author: Copilot
body: `actions/checkout` for `gh-pages` is marked `continue-on-error: true`, but the next step unconditionally runs `git commit` and `git push origin gh-pages`. If the checkout fails (e.g., branch doesn’t exist or transient failure), this can end up pushing whatever branch is currently checked out to `gh-pages`, potentially overwriting it. Make the checkout fail the job, or add an explicit guard that verifies `HEAD` is on `gh-pages` (and that the branch exists) before deleting/committing/pushing.

author: Copilot
body: `publish_coverage_to_pages` deletes and recreates `coverage/pr-$PR_NUMBER` unconditionally, but backend/frontend coverage artifacts are only produced when their respective `paths-filter` flags are true. When a job is skipped due to no changes, this publish job can still run (job result is still `success`) and deploy empty directories, leaving broken links. Consider propagating `backend_changed`/`frontend_changed` as job outputs and gating this job (and/or the directory deletion) on at least one report actually existing.

author: Copilot
body: This job uses `continue-on-error: true` for artifact downloads and for the `git push`, but still posts “View Report” links. If downloads/push fail, reviewers get URLs that 404 while the workflow still appears green. Prefer failing the job when the expected `index.html` files aren’t present after download (or generate a placeholder `index.html` per missing report), and only post the links comment after a successful push.

author: Copilot
body: Mapping *all* 400 Bad Request responses to `ResourceNotFound` can misclassify real client errors (e.g., schema/contract changes) as “not found”. Other methods in this client map 400s conditionally based on response content; consider doing the same here (e.g., check for a known “filer not found” message/code) and otherwise re-raise `HTTPStatusError`.

author: Copilot
body: `publish_coverage_to_pages` runs on the `pull_request` event but requests `contents: write` (and posts PR comments). On PRs from forks this commonly fails due to the read-only token, and more broadly it’s risky to grant write permissions in a PR-triggered workflow. Consider gating this job to same-repo PRs only (e.g., `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`), or moving the gh-pages publish to a safer event (e.g., `workflow_run` / `pull_request_target` with strict controls).

author: Copilot
body:
The gh-pages deploy step does a plain `git push origin gh-pages` without handling non-fast-forward updates. Concurrent workflow runs (or other gh-pages updates) can cause the push to fail and mark the PR checks red. Consider adding a small retry with `git pull --rebase` (or a concurrency group keyed by PR number with `cancel-in-progress: true`) before pushing, or otherwise making the push resilient.
```suggestion

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git push origin gh-pages; then
              exit 0
            fi

            if [ "$attempt" -eq 3 ]; then
              echo "❌ Failed to push to gh-pages after ${attempt} attempts"
              exit 1
            fi

            echo "Push rejected, rebasing on latest origin/gh-pages and retrying (attempt ${attempt})..."
            git pull --rebase origin gh-pages
          done
```

author: Copilot
body: The workflow downloads coverage artifacts produced from PR code, then writes placeholder HTML into the extracted directories via `cat > "${dir}/index.html"`. If an artifact contains a symlinked directory (or unexpected path structure), this redirection could write outside the intended `coverage/pr-<n>` tree. Before generating placeholders/committing, add a sanitization step to remove symlinks (and/or validate the extracted tree is regular files/dirs under `coverage/pr-${PR_NUMBER}` only).

author: Copilot
body:
`actions/checkout` of `gh-pages` is marked `continue-on-error: true`, but the job then proceeds and may silently skip cleanup if checkout fails (e.g., transient GitHub outage). Consider capturing the checkout step outcome and explicitly short-circuiting (or failing) when the branch should exist but cannot be checked out, so stale coverage reports don’t accumulate unnoticed.
```suggestion
      - name: Checkout gh-pages branch
        id: checkout_gh_pages
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: gh-pages
          fetch-depth: 1
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Fail if gh-pages checkout did not succeed
        if: steps.checkout_gh_pages.outcome != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "❌ Failed to checkout the gh-pages branch; aborting cleanup so stale coverage reports are not silently left behind."
          exit 1

      - name: Remove coverage report for this PR
        if: steps.checkout_gh_pages.outcome == 'success'
```

body: PR title/description indicates this change is about handling “filer not found”, but the PR also introduces substantial CI behavior changes (publishing coverage HTML to GitHub Pages and adding a cleanup workflow). Consider updating the PR description to cover the workflow changes (or splitting the CI changes into a separate PR) so reviewers can assess risk and intent appropriately.

author: Copilot
body: `publish_coverage_to_pages` deploys coverage to the root of GitHub Pages and explicitly notes that each deployment replaces the previous one. That makes the PR coverage links unstable (they will point to whatever PR ran last) while the landing page/title and PR comments reference a specific PR number. Consider publishing under a PR-specific subpath (e.g., `pr-<number>/...`) or adjusting the messaging/comments so it’s clear the links are not PR-scoped (and avoid embedding the PR number in the site title).

author: Copilot
body: `post_coverage_comment` hard-codes `PAGES_URL: https://nasuni.github.io/portal`, but the Pages URL is already available from `actions/deploy-pages` (`steps.deploy.outputs.page_url`) in the publishing job. Hard-coding the URL makes the workflow brittle if the repo name/org or Pages base URL changes; consider passing the deployed `page_url` through as a job output and using that in the comment builder.

Consider splitting the workflow changes into a separate PR or updating the PR description to explain the motivation/risk of the CI changes.

author: Copilot
body:
The `ResourceNotFound` raise/message is duplicated across the 404 and the special-case 400 branch. This makes it easy for the branches to drift (e.g., message changes applied to one path but not the other). Consider consolidating into a single boolean (e.g., `is_missing_filer`) and raise `ResourceNotFound(...)` once based on that condition, then `raise` for all other cases.
```suggestion
            is_missing_filer = e.response.status_code == HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND
            if e.response.status_code == HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST:
                body = e.response.text.lower()
                is_missing_filer = str(filer_id).lower() in body and "not found" in body
            if is_missing_filer:
                raise ResourceNotFound(f"Filer with ID {filer_id} not found") from e
```
